item.title: Disney’s Unwatchable New Fantasy Movie is a Sloppy Harry Potter-The Incredibles Mash-Up
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic animated film review; lacks prestige or genuine anticipation.] Hexed is packed with nods to better stories
item.content:encoded: Hexed kicks off with a standard exposition dump explaining that Hexe was formed as a sanctuary for persecuted witches and wizards. Their realm is protected by a magical spell meant to be empowered through a ritual that the extra-special “chosen witch” will complete during an upcoming lunar event. Billie Doe (Hailee Steinfeld) opened a portal to Hexe when she was a baby, and her overprotective mom Alice (Rashida Jones) has been suppressing her daughter’s powers ever since. But when Billie accidentally regains her abilities and travels to Hexe, she runs afoul of its villainous ruler Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster).

item.title: Pokémon Go 'Twilight Wishes' event guide
item.dc:creator: Julia Lee
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's everything you need to know about Pokémon Go's "Twilight Wishes" event, including how to get the sun and moon crown Pikachu.
item.content:encoded: Pokémon Go’s "Twilight Wishes" event is here to wrap up the "Twilight Trails" season. Running from Nov. 24-30, this event brings back the Pokémon featured in the previous events throughout the season, and marks the return of Espeon and Umbreon in their themed scarfs, as well as Pikachu in their sun and moon crowns.

item.title: Pokémon’s Hyped Countdown Might Be Leading to a Letdown
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon non-game news; music video announcement lacks substance.] Pokémon's social media has counting down toward something happening on Nov. 30, and it looks like the announcement will just be a music video.
item.content:encoded: In October and early November, The Pokémon Company started counting down toward the end of the month, as noted by Serebii webmaster Joe Merrick. Using Poké Ball-themed logos created for the franchise's 30th anniversary, Pokémon teased some sort of announcement for Nov. 30 at 14:00 UTC.

item.title: Avengers: Doomsday Officially Skips Awards Screenings to Avoid Spoiler Leaks
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise Marvel churn; casting/set gossip tier content.] Marvel’s Avengers: Doomsday is skipping the BAFTAs and Golden Globes to preserve spoilers ahead of release
item.content:encoded: Don't expect to see Avengers: Doomsday show up on the nomination lists at some of Hollywood's biggest awards shows in the coming months. That's because Disney and Marvel are taking extreme precautions to protect the intimate details of their upcoming superhero blockbuster, going so far as to withhold screeners in hopes of avoiding plot leaks. Still, this strategy won't dash all of Doomsday's award hopes.

item.title: James Cameron’s Sci-Fi Sequel Masterpiece Is Officially Being Removed from Netflix
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming departure notice; James Cameron prestige doesn't override this format.] James Cameron’s 1986 film Aliens is about to leave Netflix. Watch is and relive the epicfinal battle with the alien queen
item.content:encoded: In an action movie, there’s nothing worse than an underwhelming final battle. While Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings was one of the best post-Avengers: Endgame movies of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, its final battle became a disconnected CGI fest that was hard to follow. For Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Secret of the Ooze, the sequel’s fun energy was undermined when a mutated Shredder died after collapsing a dock onto himself without a fight ever even starting.

item.title: 25 Years Later, GTA 3 Is Still the Most Fascinating Open-World Experiment
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective; '25 years later' format is tossable filler.] Rockstar's 2001 GTA 3 changed the open-world game forever with its urban playground of Liberty City.
item.content:encoded: The artwork’s nothing to write home about, just a collage of pictures in red, blue, and green hues, featuring obscure faces, a police chopper, and a car up in flames. Your instinct is to just go with your gut; Silent Hill 2 is what you came here for, after all. But something’s telling you otherwise. Maybe it’s the store clerk going on about its open-world premise, or the name itself that strikes a chord within you. Whatever reason incites it, you make the ultimate decision. Little did you know, you’d be walking home with one of the greatest achievements in video game history.

item.title: Where to find the Port Gellhorn serial killer in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Finding Gelhorn's missing tourists in GTA 6 takes requires some careful sleuthing, but if you need help, here's where to look for the missing tourists
item.content:encoded: Finding Port Gelhorn's missing tourists and the serial killer in Grand Theft Auto 6 takes you on a twisted journey around the town, one with few guideposts and a lot of chances to get stuck. It's a macabre scavenger hunt with only a few pictures and knowledge of the surrounding area to go by, though the reward at the end is comparatively small. This is a quest where the storytelling, more than anything else, is the reward.

item.title: Every Playable Video Game in GTA 6, Ranked Worst to Best
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: [Filtered: Ranking/list article; similar to tier lists, not substantive analysis.] Grand Theft Auto 6 features four playable video games within the game. Here's how they stack up.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6 is so big that it’s actually five games in one. Like previous games in the series, there are several games-within-the-game that you can play while hanging out in Leonida. These aren’t just quick arcade games that you can play for a few minutes, but full-on console games that are actually pretty fun in their own right.

item.title: 'Dealer's Choice' mission choices and outcomes in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Marloes Valentina Stella
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] 'Dealer's Choice' is a mission in GTA 6 that makes you choose between pure or cut substances. Here are the 'Dealer's Choice' outcomes explained.
item.content:encoded: Choosing between pure or cut drugs in Grand Theft Auto 6 is tough; on the one hand, it'll be nice to make extra money… But on the other hand, shady dealings often end in shootouts. More than other GTA 6 missions, the "Dealer's Choice" mission in Chapter 3 has a "best" and a "worst" way to handle things.

item.title: Where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's where to find the Silent Hill hotel in GTA 6, and how to open the safe inside the haunted Marbelle Hotel
item.content:encoded: The Silent Hill hotel is one of the secrets you can stumble upon in Grand Theft Auto 6. Like the meeting with Dave and Beelzebub, you can miss the chance to enter this specific hotel and experience the creepy event that takes place inside. From the outside, it looks like a regular building, but after you visit this place, Leonida will literally change for a while. Besides, there's a safe waiting for you to open and a unique reward to collect.

item.title: Naruto Movie Officially Casts Fan-favorite Actor for Key Role
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: [Filtered: Naruto anime adaptation casting news; anime excluded from interests.] Hiroyuki Sanada has been cast in the live-action Naruto movie from Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton.
item.content:encoded: Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton is gearing up for his next live-action adaptation of an iconic franchise. He's writing and directing a live-action Naruto movie, and is in the process of casting an important role.

item.title: Where to find the UFO dream house in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] This guide explains where to find the house that is depicted on planet Earth during the UFO dream sequence in GTA 6.
item.content:encoded: If you're looking for the UFO dream house location in Grand Theft Auto 6, that means you've already seen the UFO itself once. This unmarked optional mission begins when you investigate an abandoned car at the side of the road, follow a trail of clothes strewn on the floor, then discover a woman in a rather unfortunate situation, being beamed up into the sky. The next time you go to sleep, a concerning dream sequence happens, with one part of it showing somewhere in Leonida depicted onto what is supposed to be planet Earth.

item.title: Should you give the statue to Benedict Halifax during 'Dubious Provenance' in GTA 6?
item.dc:creator: Marloes Valentina Stella
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's what happens if you give or withhold the statue from Benedict Halifax in GTA 6, as well as how to deal with him later on in the mission.
item.content:encoded: Giving the statue to Halifax during the Grand Theft Auto 6 "Dubious Provenance" mission may not seem like the wisest choice, but don't be too quick to decide. In this GTA 6 mission, one choice is more rewarding and more time-efficient than the other.

item.title: 32 Years Later, The Best 'Peanuts' Rerun Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Classic
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, matches toss pattern.] He just got here and he's already confused
item.content:encoded: Every comic strip has an evolutionary arc. Every cartoonist changes their style over time as they hone their craft, develop their sense of humor shifts, master their particular style, and/or pander to their audience. Sometimes an early character may all but disappear from the comic, or some incidental member of the cast may take up the spotlight. It's part of the fun of going on archive binges, whether it's old newspaper comics or long-running web series. Comics are living things, and few of them stay in the places where they started.

item.title: Robert Pattinson's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Thriller Proves He's a Perfect James Bond
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Generic film recommendation lacking real substance; not horror.] The Lighthouse, which is available on HBO Max, is the perfect film for the Robert Pattinson skeptic
item.content:encoded: Not everybody is convinced Robert Pattinson is the right choice to be the next James Bond. Some are complaining Bond should be played by someone less famous, like he has in the past. Others feel he’s not masculine enough, or good-looking enough, or charismatic enough. Most of all, though, it seems many people don't love the idea that “the Twilight guy” is playing Bond.

item.title: 34 Years Later, the Best 'Far Side' Quote Will Still Leave You Speechless
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old comic strip, matches toss pattern.] Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was known for its visual humor, but this is the best-ever quote from the series
item.content:encoded: Larson didn’t do deep and inspirational. Many of his cartoons required you to think, but not because they were thoughtful. Larson’s work was brilliant, and it sometimes took a few minutes to figure out what the punchline was. Take, this comic strip where an artist is painting a woman as a half-fly creature, for example. You likely see the woman or the painting first, and you wonder why the artist is painting her that way. Only after inspecting the comic more closely do you see the dead fly stuck to his glasses.

item.title: Star Wars Is Getting an Official IMAX 70mm Release for the First Time
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars big-franchise churn; theatrical rerelease is filler.] In 2027, the original untouched Star Wars will return to movie theaters — and in IMAX 70mm screenings for the first time, Lucasfilm confirms.
item.content:encoded: Han will shoot first in 70 mm IMAX when the original Star Wars returns to movie theaters next year. Lucasfilm and IMAX have confirmed that the 50th anniversary rerelease of Star Wars will be on the biggest screens possible next February, giving fans a strong reason to return to theaters.

item.title: GTA 6 Is Getting Review Bombed in Zelda vs. GTA Troll War
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: [Filtered: Fan drama and culture war clickbait, not substantive game news.] Grand Theft Auto 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time fans are fighting over Metacritic scores as part of a larger anti-woke culture war.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6 may be the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, and may have earned a record-breaking $3.79 billion on launch day, but that doesn't mean Rockstar Games' new blockbuster can't have its haters. Multiple groups have descended on GTA 6's Metacritic page to attack the game for its perceived shortcomings, much of that criticism is based on culture war nonsense.

item.title: Netflix’s (Very) R-Rated 45-Episode Sci-Fi Anthology Doesn’t Get the Attention It Deserves
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Generic streaming recommendation, not prestige project or horror.] This genre-blend anthology boasts exceptionally well-crafted episodes.
item.content:encoded: Almost four decades after the film’s release, filmmakers David Fincher and Tim Miller attempted to reboot Heavy Metal, which eventually morphed into the Netflix sci-fi anthology, Love, Death & Robots. Although the series inevitably carries the DNA of Heavy Metal and its contemporaries, Love, Death & Robots carves out its distinct identity over 45 exceptional episodes. While sci-fi is at the heart of these anthology tales, the show blends everything from horror to comedy to complement the bountiful art styles that are a celebration of animation as a medium.

item.title: 25 Years Later, Dragon Quest’s Island-Hopping Epic Gets Better in Every Port
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective framed as anniversary piece without new sequel.] The years have been kind to one classic Dragon Quest game, even if it got a slow start.
item.content:encoded: The Dragon Quest franchise has been around for longer than some of us have been alive, and its first entry in 1986 was one of the JRPG genre’s pioneers. Over the years, the launch of a new title in the series has been a big deal, especially in Japan. Before players missed work to play Grand Theft Auto 6, they were using sick days to topple wicked dragonlords.

item.title: How to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] Here's what you need to do to steal the BF Bandito in GTA 6 and complete one of Moses's requests
item.content:encoded: You need to find a way to steal the BF Bandito in Grand Theft Auto 6 to help out Moses. After completing the first batch of requests, Moses will contact you about other cars he wants you to retrieve for him. Among them is this off-road beast. Unlike the Declasse Vamos, you won't need to figure out how to move the BF Bandito out of a garage. The challenge this time is to actually make the target stop.

item.title: American Psycho Reboot Is 'Not Happening,' Director Says
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: [Filtered: Film reboot news without substantial prestige project details.] We won't be getting a version of American Psycho from the director of Challengers
item.content:encoded: A couple of years ago, reports emerged that Challengers and Call Me By Your Name director Luca Guadagnino was working on his own reimagining of American Psycho, the 2000 film adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' novel. Unfortunately (or fortunately, depending on your point of view), it doesn't appear his new take on the cult-hit psychological thriller will see the light of day.

item.title: Go on a trip with Dave and Beezlebub for a sick boss fight in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] In this guide, you learn all you need to start the Hell event in GTA 6 and go fight demons in Doom style to earn a unique weapon.
item.content:encoded: The Hell event in GTA 6 proves that you never know where a wild night in Leonidas can take you. On a quiet street, you might come across Dave and Beelzebub hanging out in a garage and listening to some rock. After a quick chat, you will learn that both of them are followers of Satan and enthusiasts of non-human vocalists in metal bands. If you stay around long enough, the two guys will invite you to take part in a special ritual, giving you the chance to start a unique event in the game.

item.title: Christopher Nolan's Mystery Thriller Masterpiece Is Officially Being Removed from Netflix
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming removal clickbait, not genuine film news.] The director's 2001 breakthrough film established many of the techniques and themes he's used throughout his career
item.content:encoded: There are common elements that define a Christopher Nolan’s movie: the presence of Cillian Murphy, a Hans Zimmer score, and visual spectacle best seen on an IMAX screen. But the element that repeats itself the most is the director's obsession with time as both a storytelling device and filmmaking trick.

item.title: Sunrise on the Reaping Makes Hunger Games A Box Office Blockbuster Franchise Again
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.category: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
item.description: [Filtered: Generic franchise box office news without substance.] Sunrise on the Reaping had a strong opening box office haul this weekend, re-establishing The Hunger Games as a box office giant.
item.content:encoded: The opening weekend box office estimates for The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping are in, and it's off to a strong start. While The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes had a somewhat muted opening in 2023 compared to the franchise's original films, Sunrise on the Reaping has had the best opening weekend of any movie released this November.

item.title: 7 Most Unforgettable Battles in Fantasy Books, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not video games or prestige content.] Some fantasy battles stay with you forever, and these unforgettable clashes prove why.
item.content:encoded: From Robert Jordan and Steven Erikson to David Gemmell and George R.R. Martin, fantasy authors have spent decades imagining conflicts that test their characters' courage, reshape entire kingdoms, and leave readers picking their jaws up off the floor in the aftermath. Consider this the definitive ranking of fantasy fiction's greatest battles, highlighting the unforgettable clashes that set the standard for warfare.

item.title: 30 Years Later, Sean Connery's Secret James Bond Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait about free movie availability.] Michael Bay’s 1996 thriller The Rock is currently free to stream. 30 years later, its still an exciting ride.
item.content:encoded: Back in the 1990s, Michael Bay was really cooking. Before the slog that was 2001’s Pearl Harbor and his divisive Transformers movies that simultaneously hurt and enhanced his career by sidelining him for decades, Bay debuted as a director with a trio of really exciting movies that prioritized a fun experience for the viewer. First there was 1995’s Bad Boys, the Will Smith and Martin Lawrence buddy-cop film that became a popular franchise. He closed out the decade with the genre-defining end-of-the-world disaster filmArmageddon. And in between those two, he gave us a tightly crafted thriller that is currently free to stream (with ads) on Pluto TV.

item.title: Star Wars’ 2-Part Sci-Fi War Thriller Has One of the Best Seasons in TV History
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars franchise TV news, falls under big-franchise churn.] Disney needed a win for one specific franchise, and Tony Gilroy gave Star Wars just that with the first season of 'Andor.'
item.content:encoded: In 2022, Disney was having a pretty strange year with its franchises. There were some major wins, such as the hugely financially successful release of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness and Turning Red becoming a streaming hit. Its films also earned $4.9 billion at the box office that year.

item.title: 8 Best Science Fantasy Books of the 21st Century
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: [Filtered: Generic book list, not gaming or prestige content.] Break genre barriers with spacefaring necromancers and aliens employing goblins. Here are some of the best sci-fi fantasy books.
item.content:encoded: The legendary science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke once said, “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” The lines between sci-fi and fantasy blur in popular entertainment franchises like Star Wars, Warhammer 40,000, and the Marvel Cinematic Universe, as well as in classic book series like Dune and Dragonriders of Pern. If you’re looking for a new world to explore and can’t decide if you want it filled with spaceships or dragons, you don’t necessarily have to choose. Just pick something from this list of the best science fantasy books of the 21st century.

item.title: 29 years later, Homer’s Best ‘The Simpsons’ Quote is Still Pure Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective (29 years later), not new content.] Homer Simpson’s best quote from The Simpsons came during season 8 and contains some profoubd wisdom
item.content:encoded: Personally, my favorite-ever quote from Homer Simpson came during season 4 of The Simpsons, in an episode named “Whacking Day.” The episode is about the citizens of Springfield celebrating a local holiday named Whacking Day, when they lure all the snakes in Springfield to the center of town and then beat them to death with baseball bats. Everyone loves this holiday except Lisa Simpson, who finds it to be cruel.

item.title: 'Calvin and Hobbes' Best Bully Quote Is Still Among the Wisest in Comic Strip History
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about vintage comic strip quote.] Moe was Calvin’s big dumb bully in Calvin and Hobbes. Here is his best quote from the beloved comic strip.
item.content:encoded: In the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Calvin often defines his babysitter Rosalyn as his arch-nemesis. He regularly plots against her and tries to sabotage her relationship with her boyfriend. He even locked her out of the house once while she was babysitting him, which got him into big trouble with his parents.

item.title: 46 Years Later, the Most Influential Thriller of All Time Is Officially Free on YouTube
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] The start of Jason Voorhees's story, 'Friday the 13th,' is now available to watch for free.
item.content:encoded: Over the years, corporations and filmmakers alike have eagerly sought to revisit the origins of horror classics (e.g., Bates Motel and Psycho, Welcome to Derry and IT, etc.) for modern audiences. It’s an easy way to find successwhen you already have an audience that loves the IP you’re reimagining

item.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
item.dc:creator: Terry Terrones
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show; not substance-based news.] Captain Kirk's speech in 'Return to Tomorrow' says more about what Star Trek stands for than any other line in the original series.
item.content:encoded: Some lines of dialogue become so famous they stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context and permeated the pop culture zeitgeist.

item.title: 61 Years Later, Charlie Brown's Greatest Enemy Is Still an Undefeated 'Peanuts' Icon
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about comic strip; not Polygon's core focus.] Charlie Brown's only real arch-rival was a malevolent tree. Chomp chomp chomp.
item.content:encoded: Like many comics aimed at children, Charles Schulz's Peanuts doesn't have too many actual villains. It has a number of antagonists, such as Lucy Van Pelt, various other kids, or the impersonal cloud of failure that constantly hangs over Charlie Brown's head, but it's rare to see a genuinely malevolent force in Peanuts — with one exception.

item.title: Star Wars' New Jedi Order Era is Officially Moving Forward
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: [Filtered: Star Wars casting/production gossip falls under big-franchise churn.] Two upcoming Star Wars films, New Jedi Order and Lucasfilm head Dave Filoni's untitled project, are making progress.
item.content:encoded: Despite Star Wars: The Mandalorian & Grogu struggling at the box office, it seems Disney is continuing development on two upcoming Star Wars films. This summer, Star Wars: New Jedi Order and Dave Filoni’s untitled movie as in-development projects were confirmed to be in the works in industry publication Production Weekly, suggesting that despite delays and silence around the projects, they haven't been shelved.

item.title: Where to find the giant crab safe code and Crabshack VF5 SMG in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] GTA 6's giant crab event takes you through Pelican Valley Outpost and rewards you with the Crabshack VF5 SMG standout weapon.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6has a giant crab haunting the swamps and, more importantly, the Crabshack VF5 SMG, a crab-themed gun, to help your future career prospects. It's all part of an optional event called Pelican Valley Outpost that sees you pick up the pieces of some questionable experiments carried out on behalf of a store chain. It's worth the trouble, even aside from the standout weapon. There's some cash to help reach your next family fund milestone and a free jet ski, too. Best of all, this little excursion is completely safe, assuming you don't run afoul of the local gator population.

item.title: Declasse Vamos code location in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Johnny Yu
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] The Declasse Vamos is inside a locked garage in GTA 6. Here's where to find the keypad code and what it is.
item.content:encoded: The Declasse Vamos is a car that you can steal for Moses in Grand Theft Auto 6. However, when you find the Declasse Vamos, you realize that it's locked away inside a garage, and you need to find the door code to get to it.

item.content:encoded: Director Bassam Tariq, who was previously attached to direct the Mahershala Ali Blade movie that never came to fruition, was candid that the lack of a strong, complete script caused the Marvel Cinematic Universe movie to fall apart before it even started shooting.

item.title: How to use auto drive in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] GTA 6's auto drive feature lets you enjoy the sights and sounds of Vice City without driving manually. Here's how to use auto drive in GTA 6.
item.content:encoded: Grand Theft Auto 6's auto drive feature is perfect if you just want to see the sights of Leonida or avoid navigating through traffic. Not that GTA 6 goes out of its way to tell you there even is an auto drive feature. It's tucked away in a menu you have little cause to use early in the game, and you also need to make sure a specific setting is toggled on for it to work in some circumstances. It's best to still learn how to drive decently yourself, though, as auto drive isn't the best choice in hectic situations.

item.title: Apple TV’s New 8-Part Crime Thriller Is Already a No. 1 Streaming Hit
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: [Filtered: Streaming clickbait about generic TV success ranking.] Apple TV’s 12 12 12 follows a bank robbery across three timelines and has quickly become a streaming sensation.
item.content:encoded: Anthony Mackie has spent decades building an impressive Hollywood career, moving between blockbuster franchises, action movies, and acclaimed television projects. From playing Sam Wilson in the Marvel Cinematic Universe to starring in The Hurt Locker and 8 Mile, Mackie has become a familiar face to audiences across several genres.

item.title: Where to find the bowling alley safe code in GTA 6
item.dc:creator: Ford James
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: category "Guides"] The Kingpin Bowling Alley in GTA 6 is home to a locked safe. Here's where you can find the code and what you can find inside.
item.content:encoded: The Kingpin Bowling Alley safe code in Grand Theft Auto 6 is, frustratingly, not actually in the bowling alley itself. No, to get your hands on it legitimately, you need to ransack a different Kolt & Associates illegal operation, which essentially acts as the gang's headquarters, and has multiple safe codes available at once. But that doesn't help when you're deep in the back offices of the bowling alley, and you're being shot at by dozens of angry gang members.

item.title: 5 Years Later, 'Yellowjackets' Officially Solves One of Its Last Huge Mysteries
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV series mystery reveal; not prestige/horror/game-related.] The location where the Yellowjackets crash-landed has been a hot topic of discussion for years. 'Yellowjackets' season 4 has the answers.
item.content:encoded: Yellowjackets has plenty of mysteries that have yet to be answered as the twisty survival thriller reaches its final season. Is the show supernatural or just a psychological thriller? Are there more adult Yellowjackets still alive? What does the symbol the teen Yellowjackets keep finding in the wilderness mean?

item.title: George R.R. Martin’s 7 Best Non-Game of Thrones Books, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Graphic-novel/book promo excerpt; not game-related content.] From antebellum Mississippi vampires to cat-loving space traders, George R.R. Martin’s best work goes far beyond Westeros and Game of Thrones.
item.content:encoded: George R.R. Martin will forever be associated with his book series, A Song of Ice and Fire, and HBO’s adaptation, Game of Thrones, but there's considerably more to his bibliography than scheming Lannisters, fire-breathing dragons, and the unending wait for The Winds of Winter. Long before Westeros became a cultural phenomenon, Martin was building a reputation as one of science fiction and fantasy's most imaginative voices, writing everything from supernatural mysteries and vampiric thrillers to sprawling space operas and intimate character dramas.

item.title: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of old comic strip; filler content.] Gary Larson's comic strip The Far Side was at its greatest when it was really, really funny. That's why is these are his 10 best comics
item.content:encoded: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke. Because of its brevity, it's easy to trivialize the medium as simply the “funny papers,” a daily, disposable art form designed to pick you up after reading the actual news.

item.title: 9 Calvin and Hobbes Comics from the 1990s that Prove Bill Watterson is a Genius
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective of classic 1990s comic strip.] Calvin and Hobbes creator Bill Watterson is a genius. Here are nine comics which prove it.
item.content:encoded: Calvin and Hobbescreator Bill Watterson is a genius. Over the course of ten years spanning more than 3,000 comic strips, he developed two truly irresistible characters that are still beloved by millions. There was a lot behind the success of Calvin and Hobbes, but I think part of the reason why Watterson is still so widely respected is that he was an incredibly versatile artist who managed to do a lot of different things in an artform that can sometimes be limiting.

item.title: 8 Near-Perfect Fantasy Miniseries That Hook You in the First Episode
item.dc:creator: Ryan Epps
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV series list without prestige project or horror substance.] From gothic castles to hidden London underworlds, these essential fantasy miniseries cast an instant spell on viewers from episode one.
item.content:encoded: Fantasy television has given us some of the most imaginative stories ever told, transporting viewers to magical kingdoms, mysterious alternate realities, and worlds filled with creatures that shouldn't exist. Shows like Game of Thrones and Rings of Power dominate the conversation, pushing some of the genre's best storytelling to the forefront, but there’s something to be said of the smaller productions and shorter stories.
